# SOOS — Multi-Agent Delegation (MAD)
# draft-sato-soos-mad-03
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/mad/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: 5 July 2026

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

MAD (Multi-Agent Delegation) is the kernel-enforced delegation and cluster governance protocol for concurrent SOOS agent sessions. Version -03 adds the Sub-Agent Composition Record (SACR) for kernel-governed sub-agent spawning, the hub-only constraint for sub-agent communication topology, XPID cross-cluster integration for cross-boundary delegation audit, and full normative per-trigger specifications for the R-1 through R-7 revocation trigger classes including completion state and cascade behavior matrices.

MAD is NOT a general-purpose authorization framework, a token-passing protocol, or a scoping mechanism for API access. It governs the full lifecycle of a multi-agent delegation tree: how it is created (SACR), how it operates (INV-4 Narrowing, hub-only, cluster coordination), and how it ends (R-1 through R-7 revocation with completion state).

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without MAD-03, your multi-agent system additionally lacks:

- A kernel-witnessed record of sub-agent spawning — today's sub-agent creation is an unaudited LLM API call with a scoped system prompt; SACR provides a kernel-signed, GAR-recorded composition event before the sub-agent executes its first action
- A tool-subset invariant check at spawn time — a spawning agent can currently grant a sub-agent broader tool access than it holds; the GEC atomically validates this at SACR issuance
- Hub-only coordination — sub-agents that communicate directly create ungoverned state changes invisible to the Mission Status SO and the kernel; hub-only requires all coordination to route through the kernel-governed hub
- XPID-based delegation tree reconstruction across GEC boundaries — without XPID chaining, cross-cluster audit requires full audit log disclosure between domains
- Per-trigger normative depth for R-1 through R-7 — MAD-02 named the triggers but lacked completion state matrices and cascade behavior specifications

---

## SECTION 3 — Key Normative Concepts

SACR (Sub-Agent Composition Record):  [NEW in -03]
   The kernel-issued record governing Mechanism B sub-agent spawning. Issued by the GEC (not the agent) before the sub-agent executes its first action. Key fields: sacr_id (UUID v4), parent_assignment_id, parent_session_id, parent_mandate_id, parent_xpid, ephemeral_kia_ref (UUID v4, session-scoped), scope_constraints (tool_subset, cedar_action_subset, resource_envelope, so_type_scope), can_decompose (boolean, default false), max_spawn_depth (integer, strictly decrements per recursion level), hub_only (boolean, default true), replan_authority (NONE/BOUNDED/AUTONOMOUS, default NONE), sacr_signature (GEC Ed25519).
   SACR is committed to GAR as ALE-SPAWN-01 before sub-agent execution. Distinct from Assignment (which governs what the sub-agent may do once it exists): SACR governs how it comes to exist.

ephemeral_kia_ref:  [NEW in -03]
   A session-scoped identity (UUID v4) issued by the GEC at SACR issuance for Mechanism B sub-agents. Not a persistent Party Registry entry. Valid only for the duration of the spawned sub-agent's session. Retired on session close (ALE-SPAWN-04: EPHEMERAL_IDENTITY_EXPIRED). An Assignment's assigned_agent_id for Mechanism B MUST equal the SACR's ephemeral_kia_ref.

can_decompose / max_spawn_depth:  [NEW in -03]
   can_decompose: boolean. May the spawned sub-agent itself spawn further children? Default false. A sub-agent with can_decompose: false MUST NOT call gec.spawnSubAgent(). max_spawn_depth: integer. Strictly decrements at each recursive spawn (parent's max_spawn_depth - 1 = child's ceiling). Value 0 = leaf; MUST NOT spawn. CONF-MAD-19: parent MUST NOT grant max_spawn_depth greater than (parent's own - 1).

hub_only:  [NEW in -03]
   Boolean. Default true. Sub-agents with hub_only: true MUST NOT send messages, state updates, or coordination signals directly to sibling sub-agents (CONF-MAD-HUB-01). The GEC enforces this via Cedar context.hub_only_active and by blocking Action::\"DirectSubAgentComm\" (CONF-MAD-HUB-03). Override requires hub_only: false in SACR AND explicit Cedar PERMIT AND DIRECT_COMM_PERMITTED event committed to GAR (Section 5.2). hub_only: false in a SACR issued by a hub_only: true parent is a conformance violation (CONF-MAD-HUB-04).

Sub-agent XPID:  [NEW in -03]
   Derived as UUID5(KIA_XPID_NAMESPACE, parent_xpid + ':' + sacr_id) per Section 6.1. Provides a stable, derivation-based cross-cluster sub-agent identifier that chains from root orchestrator to leaf sub-agent. Recorded in ALE-SPAWN-01 and in every GAR governance span as soos.governance.xpid. Cross-cluster verification: receiving GEC obtains SACR from originating GEC, recomputes XPID, verifies match (CONF-MAD-XPID-01, -02).

SACR Registry:  [NEW in -03]
   A kernel-internal lookup of active SACRs by session_id, used for hub-only enforcement (Section 5.3) and cross-cluster XPID verification. Rebuilt from committed ALE-SPAWN-01 events on kernel restart before any sub-agent session may execute (CONF-MAD-22).

R-1 through R-7 (full normative specs):  [UPDATED in -03]
   R-1 (CAP Tier 0-A): completion PARTIAL always; cascade FULL; human reauth required; all SACRs voided, ephemeral refs retired immediately.
   R-2 (Scope Boundary): completion CLEAN (if Cedar DENY at Step 1 before execution) / PARTIAL (if post-execution) / UNKNOWN (if execution state unknown); cascade FULL; human reauth required.
   R-3 (Non-Response): completion UNKNOWN always (treated as PARTIAL per INV-15); cascade SELECTIVE (responsive descendants continue); operator may reauth + must notify principal.
   R-4 (Irreversible Threshold): completion CLEAN (if halted before action) / PARTIAL (if post-irreversible-action); cascade FULL; human reauth required.
   R-5 (Scheduled Rotation): completion CLEAN (if natural breakpoint reached) / PARTIAL; cascade NONE (session-specific); operator may reauth; natural breakpoint wait required (CONF-MAD-R5-01).
   R-6 (Operator Override): completion CLEAN/PARTIAL; cascade per revocation_scope field; operator may reauth + must notify principal.
   R-7 (DEADLOCK): completion UNKNOWN always; cascade ALL participating sessions simultaneously; human reauth required; ephemeral refs retained pending resolution.

Completion State Matrix (Table 1 in §7.8):
   R-1: PARTIAL always.
   R-2: CLEAN (Cedar DENY Step 1) / PARTIAL / UNKNOWN.
   R-3: UNKNOWN always.
   R-4: CLEAN (pre-action) / PARTIAL.
   R-5: CLEAN (natural breakpoint) / PARTIAL.
   R-6: CLEAN (natural breakpoint) / PARTIAL.
   R-7: UNKNOWN always.

Terms carried forward from MAD-02 (no changes):
   INV-4 (Narrowing Property), INV-15 (UNKNOWN = PARTIAL), INV-16 (completion_state REQUIRED in GAR on revocation), MANDATE_HOLD, DEADLOCK, Cluster state machine (ACTIVE/CLUSTER_BLOCKED/MANDATE_HOLD/DEADLOCK/TERMINATED), cascade_timeout, five cluster collision problems, BUDGET_TRANSFER, ALE-013 through ALE-016.

---

## SECTION 4 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

KIA-03 (draft-sato-soos-kia-03):
   Sub-agent XPID derivation (Section 6.1) uses the KIA-03 XPID namespace and derivation scheme. The ephemeral_kia_ref in SACR is a session-scoped identity distinct from a persistent KIA Party Registry entry but derived under the same kernel identity infrastructure.

HEM-05 (draft-sato-soos-hem-05):
   MAD-03 §15.8 normatively references HEM-PRE-2 (pre-action confirmation for irreversible actions) as the cascade timing attack defense mechanism. HEM_MULTI_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED fires on R-7 (DEADLOCK). HEM-DIV-1 is referenced in sub-agents with replan_authority: BOUNDED for deviation surfacing.

GAR-03 (draft-sato-soos-gar-03):
   ALE-SPAWN-01 through ALE-SPAWN-04 registered in MAD-03 IANA section. Sub-agent XPID recorded as soos.governance.xpid in every GAR governance span. HUB_ONLY_VIOLATION, DIRECT_COMM_PERMITTED, IRREVERSIBLE_THRESHOLD_REACHED, SCHEDULED_ROTATION_INITIATED, SESSION_REVOKED_BY_OPERATOR, SACR_REGISTRY_REBUILT are new kernel events recorded in GAR.

DR-SPAWN-01 (June 19, 2026):
   Source document for SACR design (Section 4), hub-only constraint (OQ-SPAWN-06 resolution), tool-subset invariant (§5.1), spawn-depth invariant (§5.2), and can_decompose/max_spawn_depth/replan_authority Assignment extensions. ALE-SPAWN-01 through ALE-SPAWN-04 schemas were identified in DR-SPAWN-01 §5.3.

DR-MAD-REC-01 (June 4, 2026):
   Source document for the full R-1 through R-7 per-trigger normative specifications in Section 7. The completion state matrix and cascade behavior matrix formalize the taxonomy introduced in DR-MAD-REC-01.

---

## SECTION 5 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft depends on:
   IDP (draft-sato-soos-idp-05) — IDP declared intent for SACR tool-subset and replan_authority; HEM-DIV-1 triggers on IDP divergence
   HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-05) — CLUSTER_CASCADE_ALERT; HEM_MULTI_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED; HEM-PRE-2 for irreversible action cascade defense
   MJWT (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-02) — sub-mandate issuance; BUDGET_TRANSFER MJWT reissuance; continuation mandate predecessor_mandate_id
   KIA (draft-sato-soos-kia-03) — XPID derivation namespace; ephemeral_kia_ref issuance; cross-cluster GEC Manifest verification
   SOV (draft-sato-soos-sov-02) — Sovereign Object instances cluster agents act on
   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-03) — ALE-013 through ALE-016 (unchanged); ALE-SPAWN-01 through ALE-SPAWN-04 (new); hub and R-trigger events

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   CAP (draft-sato-soos-cap-04) — CAP applies per delegation level; R-1 trigger is a CAP Tier 0-A violation
   AEP (draft-sato-soos-aep-02) — AEP session lifecycle defers to MAD §3.6 for revocation procedure (SA-09)

Target WG engagement at IETF 126 Vienna (July 18–24, 2026):
   OAUTH WG — MAD profiles RFC 8693 (Token Exchange) for sub-mandate issuance; SACR is the kernel-layer primitive that sub-mandate issuance depends on
   SECEVENT / SSF WG — MAD §3.6.2 CAEP profile for agent-session-revoked events (first such profile for AI agent session revocation); R-1 through R-7 taxonomy is the trigger classification that feeds the CAEP event body
   GNAP WG — SACR delegation authority model has structural parallels to GNAP delegation chains
   ANML / AUDIT — hub-only constraint as the normative answer to multi-agent coordination governance; SACR audit chain as an AUDIT WG candidate record type
